messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: type inference, etc. in place
parts:
I just did a mondo commit, including all the type
inference.

I'm now checking all the models in the BUGS folders.

I had to change a few models that used multivariates. These
need to have the appropriate vector or matrix types.

I also put a model good_all.stan in the test folder
that shows how the code gets generated for lvalues
and expressions. The trick is that matrices in Eigen
need (m,n) notation, whereas everything else is [m][n].

Let me know if you see anything strange. I had
to make some substantial changes to things like
the grammar to deal with operator precedence and
push the type checking through.

Other than the R interface, this is about it for
the baseline Stan 1.0. There's still optimization
and all the truncated distributions, but that doesn't
all need to go out in 1.0.

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] type inference, etc. in place
parts:
Cool! Any estimates on when we think we'll release? It'd be good to
have a rough date to tell NIPS people.

Sorry I haven't been paying much attention to what's going on on
stan-dev, the internet situation in my hotel is pretty awful. To send
an email from my room I generally have to
1. Run 'ping www.google.es'
2. While watching the pings go by, hold my laptop aloft and find a
height/orientation at which the pings start going through
3. Switch windows and hit send.
Anyway, I want to spend a few days optimizing, but won't be able to
this week. Also, it'd be good to get the precompiled headers stuff
working if it isn't already to speed model compilation. (A different
kind of optimization.)

In other news, I've been thinking about a way of setting step sizes
using (rejectable) local adaptation in a way that preserves detailed
balance. It may or may not be practical (or indeed correct, although I
think it is), and probably shouldn't go in the first release, but it
could be cool. Not sure yet if it's only applicable/useful to/for
scalar step sizes or if it can also be used to estimate scales
locally, which would be awesome. I'll have more details when I get
back.

Matt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: release planning
parts:
No way we can release Stan 1.0 (beta?) before
January. It should be pretty stable as of yesterday
in terms of what's already done.

My list of what remains to do is:

1. user manual
2. error handling / arithmetic robustness
3. discrete sampling
4. Rstan (calls, convergence, ESS)
5. make JAGS Rats model faster
6. 30 or so more BUGS models
7. paper

I'm pretty sure Daniel and I can knock out 1 and 2
in a week or two.

We need to talk more about 3.

4 should be reasonably easy, especially with help from
Malecki. Most of the connections are in place, but we
also need to test cross-platform.

I don't know what to do about 5 given. Maybe Andrew
will relent when we show a bunch of models for
which Stan is faster.

The risk with 6 is that the models will expose
problems with everything else.

Maybe we can punt on 7 until after the release.

Daniel tried to get precompiled headers working without
any luck -- if you (Matt) can help out, that'd be great.

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] release planning
parts:
I've got some (not checked in or tested) default code that does
discrete sampling using slice sampling, which should at least be
reasonably robust. Someday we'll probably want to try to figure out
what depends on what so that we can do Gibbs without recomputing
everything, but that can wait.

And I'll take a look at precompiling headers when I get back.

Matt
